mainTopic: The tall סוכה of הילני המלכה, the minimum size of a סוכה (head, most of the body, and table), and a house smaller than four by four אמות
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the story of הילני המלכה and her סוכה taller than twenty אמות. For the opinion that the dispute is about a small סוכה, it asks whether a queen would really sit in one. רב אשי answers that her סוכה was large but had small side-rooms. The רבנן say only she sat in those rooms, while רבי יהודה says her sons sat with her. Next, רב שמואל בר יצחק rules that a סוכה must hold a person's head, most of his body, and his table, and he admits that this follows בית שמאי. רב נחמן בר יצחק suggests that בית שמאי and בית הלל really argue about a large סוכה whose owner's table is in the house. Two ברייתות and the wording of the משנה show they also argue about a small סוכה's size, so the גמרא concludes they argue about both cases. Finally, the גמרא asks which תנא holds that a house smaller than four by four אמות does not count as a house, and it begins listing the laws that do not apply to such a house.

steps.title: A queen sits in an airy סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of an earlier answer: a queen would sit in a סוכה with openings because of the fresh air.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that started before this section. A queen would choose a סוכה with openings in its walls because of the fresh air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא keeps asking whether הילני המלכה, a queen, would really have sat in the kind of סוכה each opinion describes. Here it explains that an airy סוכה with openings fits a queen's comfort, so that reading of the story works.

keyTerms.meaning: air, fresh air

phrases.english: Because of the air.
phrases.notes: This finishes the answer from just before: openings in the walls let in a nice breeze, which suits a queen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the previous answer, which began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the case fits a queen's lifestyle
steps.terutzMaskana: A queen would sit in an airy סוכה, so that reading of the story holds up.

steps.title: Would a queen sit in a small סוכה?
steps.stepSummary: Against the opinion that the dispute is about a small סוכה, the גמרא asks whether a queen would ever sit in one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says the dispute is about a small סוכה: is it a queen's way to sit in a small סוכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to another opinion, which says the dispute is about a small סוכה. It challenges that opinion: a queen would not sit in a tiny סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument is only about a small סוכה, then the story of הילני must be about a small סוכה. But it is hard to picture a queen with a large household sitting in a cramped booth. So this reading seems not to fit the story.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the one who says
a small סוכה (about the minimum size)
a dispute
is it really her way / normal practice?

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
the dispute is about a small sukka,
is it really the way of a queen
to sit in a small sukka?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as before, now aimed at a different opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that the dispute about a tall סוכה applies only to a small סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under this opinion, the story of הילני must be about a small סוכה. A queen would not normally sit in one.

steps.title: A סוכה divided into small rooms
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב אדא answers that her סוכה was large but split into many small rooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב אדא said: It is needed only for a סוכה made of many small rooms.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב אדא answers the question. Her סוכה was big overall, but it was divided into many little rooms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each small room counts as a small סוכה on its own, so the dispute about a small סוכה applies. Yet the whole building was large enough to suit a queen.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for (this case)
small rooms or compartments

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Adda said:
It is needed only
for a sukka made of many small rooms.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: We pictured one tiny סוכה, which does not suit a queen.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a big סוכה split into small rooms. Each room is small, but the whole place suits a queen.

steps.title: Would a queen sit where it is only small rooms?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: would a queen use a סוכה that has only small rooms and no large one?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it a queen's way to sit in a סוכה made of many small rooms?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of רבה בר רב אדא. A queen would still want a big room, not just small ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting the סוכה into rooms solves the size problem only on paper. A queen with her family and servants would need a large space to gather. So the answer still does not fit her lifestyle.

phrases.english: Is it really the way of a queen to sit
in a sukka made of many small rooms?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דַּרְכָּהּ שֶׁל מַלְכָּה לֵישֵׁב בְּסוּכָּה הָעֲשׂוּיָה קִיטוֹנִיּוֹת קִיטוֹנִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 3 using the same kind of question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב אדא's picture of a סוכה made entirely of small rooms
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A queen would not settle for a סוכה made only of small rooms with no large room.

steps.title: A large סוכה with small side-rooms
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the סוכה had a large main area, and the dispute is about the small rooms attached to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is needed only for the small rooms inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a better picture. The סוכה was large with a main room, and it also had small side-rooms. The dispute is about those side-rooms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the queen has a proper large space, which suits her. The dispute about a small, tall סוכה applies to the little rooms attached to the main area.

keyTerms.meaning: that are in it (inside the סוכה)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is needed only for the small rooms inside it.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole סוכה was nothing but small rooms.
steps.terutzMaskana: There was a large main area plus small side-rooms. The dispute is about the side-rooms.

steps.title: How each side reads the story
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say her sons sat in the proper main area and she sat in the side-rooms for modesty. רבי יהודה says her sons sat with her in the small rooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: her sons sat in the proper סוכה, and she sat in the small rooms for modesty, so the זקנים said nothing to her. רבי יהודה holds: her sons sat with her, and even so the זקנים said nothing to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how each side understands the story using רב אשי's picture. The question is whether the זקנים' silence proves the small rooms were כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the silence proves nothing. Her sons, who were obligated, sat in the large area, and she, a woman, is not obligated in סוכה. For רבי יהודה, her sons sat with her in the small room, so the silence shows that a small room taller than twenty אמות is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: a proper, fully valid סוכה (here, the large main area)
modesty, privacy
with her, next to her
they did not say anything to her

steps.whatToRemember: Under רב אשי's picture, both sides can read the story of הילני their own way. The difference is where her sons sat: in the big room (רבנן) or with her in the small room (רבי יהודה).
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן do not say the small rooms were כשר. They say the זקנים' silence proves nothing, because only the queen sat there and she was not obligated.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
her sons were sitting in a proper sukka,
phrases.notes: The 'proper sukka' is the large main area of her סוכה.

phrases.english: and she sat in the small rooms
for the sake of modesty,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא אָמְרִי לַהּ דָּבָר.
phrases.english: and that is why they said nothing to her.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the זקנים who visited her סוכה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
her sons were sitting with her,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא אָמְרִי לַהּ דָּבָר.
phrases.english: and even so they said nothing to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב אשי's answer and shows how each side reads the story under it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the dispute within the case
steps.terutzMaskana: The story fits both sides. They disagree about where her sons sat, so the story does not decide the law.

steps.title: A סוכה must hold head, most of the body, and table
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק rules that a סוכה must be big enough for a person's head, most of his body, and his table.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: The הלכה is that it must hold his head, most of his body, and his table.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב שמואל בר יצחק gives a practical ruling on the smallest size a סוכה may be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a minimum size. It is not enough to fit just yourself; there must also be room for your table.

keyTerms.meaning: the practical law
holds, has room for
his head and most of his body
his table

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is about the practical minimum size of a סוכה, so it matters for actually building one.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: הֲלָכָה,
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said: The halakha is,
it must be big enough to hold
his head, most of his body, and his table.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the minimum size of a סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה must hold a person's head, most of his body, and his table.

steps.title: Does this follow בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא is surprised: the ruling seems to follow בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: Like whom? Like בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא challenges the ruling. Requiring room for the table is the view of בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the הלכה follows בית הלל over בית שמאי. If only בית שמאי require room for the table, ruling that way seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: like whom? (whose opinion is this?)
the school of שמאי, whose view usually is not followed

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
Like whom? Like Beit Shammai?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמואל בר יצחק's ruling that the table must fit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling matches בית שמאי, and the הלכה normally follows בית הלל.

steps.title: Whom else would I follow?
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק answers: Rather, like whom? He accepts that his ruling follows בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Rather, like whom?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יצחק answers with a question of his own. He stands by his ruling and accepts that it follows בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not back down. In effect he says, 'Yes, like בית שמאי. Whom else would it follow?' He treats this case as one where the הלכה follows בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, like whom? (meaning: of course like them)

phrases.english: He said to him: Rather, like whom?!
phrases.notes: He means: 'Of course like בית שמאי. Whom else?'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the ruling follows בית שמאי, and he stands by it.

steps.title: A second version of the exchange: it is בית שמאי, but do not budge from it
steps.stepSummary: Some report the conversation differently. רבי אבא asks whose opinion this is, and רב שמואל בר יצחק answers that it is בית שמאי, and we should hold firmly to it anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the conversation went like this. רבי אבא asked: "Whose opinion are you telling me?" רב שמואל בר יצחק answered: "It is בית שמאי, and do not move away from it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the talk between רבי אבא and רב שמואל בר יצחק. In this version, רב שמואל בר יצחק openly says the ruling is from בית שמאי and that we hold by it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (steps 8–9), רבי אבא was surprised and רב שמואל בר יצחק simply admitted it was בית שמאי. Here רבי אבא just asks whose view it is, and the answer adds something strong: even though it is בית שמאי, this is the practical הלכה. Either way, both versions assume that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about the minimum size of a small סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Who? Whose opinion is this?
Do not budge from it; hold firmly to this ruling

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: דַּאֲמַר לָךְ מַנִּי?
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said: The one who told you this, who is it?
phrases.notes: He is asking whose opinion stands behind the ruling about head, most of the body, and table.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is Beit Shammai,
and do not budge from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: דַּאֲמַר לָךְ מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of the same exchange from steps 8–9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose opinion is the ruling that a סוכה must hold head, most of the body, and table?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is בית שמאי, and the ruling should be followed firmly.

steps.title: Maybe the dispute is about a large סוכה with the table in the house
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges the assumption that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about a small סוכה's size. Perhaps they argue about a big סוכה where a person sits at its entrance and his table is in the house. בית שמאי make a גזירה that he may be drawn after his table, and בית הלל do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objected: How do you know בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about a small סוכה? Maybe they argue about a big סוכה, where a person sits at the opening of the סוכה and his table is inside the house. בית שמאי hold that we make a decree, because he might get pulled after his table into the house. בית הלל hold that we don't make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the basic idea behind steps 7–10, that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about the minimum size of a סוכה. He offers a totally different way to read their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now everyone assumed בית שמאי require a סוכה big enough for head, most of the body, and table. רב נחמן בר יצחק says maybe the size is not the issue at all. The סוכה could be big, and the real question is whether we worry that a person whose table is in the house will slowly lean or move into the house. That makes it a dispute about a גזירה, not about size.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it: a sharp challenge
Perhaps; maybe it is different
The opening (entrance) of the סוכה
We make a גזירה, a protective rabbinic decree
Lest he be drawn after (his table)

steps.confusionAlert: In this reading, בית שמאי are not saying the סוכה is too small. The סוכה is big; their concern is only about where the person and his table are sitting.
steps.whyThisMatters: If רב נחמן בר יצחק is right, then רב שמואל בר יצחק's ruling about size may not come from בית שמאי at all.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak objected to it:
From where do you know that Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel
disagree about a small sukka?
Perhaps they disagree about a large sukka,
for example where he sits at the opening of the sukka
and his table is inside the house.
For Beit Shammai hold: We make a decree
lest he be drawn after his table,
phrases.notes: The worry is that while eating he'll drift toward his table until he's really inside the house.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel hold: We do not make a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the shared assumption behind both versions of the exchange in steps 8–10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about the minimum size of a small סוכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their argument could just as well be about a large סוכה with the table in the house, a question of a גזירה rather than of size.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports the large-סוכה reading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes someone whose head and most of his body are in the סוכה and his table in the house. If the dispute were about size, the משנה should have said "a סוכה that holds" versus "one that doesn't hold".
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording also fits this, because the משנה says: "Someone whose head and most of his body were in the סוכה and his table was inside the house: בית שמאי say it is not valid and בית הלל say it is valid." If the argument were about size, the משנה should have spoken about a סוכה that holds or doesn't hold these things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב נחמן בר יצחק from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה talks about where the person and his table are placed, not about how big the סוכה is. If the dispute were really about minimum size, the natural wording would be "a סוכה that holds head, most of the body and table" versus "one that does not." Since the משנה doesn't say that, it seems the argument is about the table being in the house.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it is also precise": the exact wording supports this
Declare invalid / declare valid
Holds; has room for
And if it were so (as you said)
It should have said

phrases.english: And it is also precise, for it teaches:
One whose head and most of his body were in the sukka
and his table was inside the house,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַכְשִׁירִין.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai declare it invalid and Beit Hillel declare it valid.
And if it were so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if the argument really were about the size of the סוכה.

phrases.english: it should have said "holds" and "does not hold."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading from step 11 using the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל is about a large סוכה with the table in the house, not about size.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording describes where the person and table are, without mentioning whether the סוכה "holds" them.

steps.title: But a ברייתא shows a real dispute about the size of a small סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: is there really no dispute about a small סוכה? A ברייתא says a סוכה that holds head, most of the body, and table is valid, while רבי requires four אמות by four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no argument about a small סוכה? But a ברייתא teaches: "A סוכה that holds his head, most of his body, and his table is valid. רבי says: it is not valid until it measures four אמות by four אמות."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against step 11's claim. It brings a ברייתא showing that there is a known argument about how small a סוכה can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 suggested that the dispute is not about the size of a small סוכה at all. This ברייתא shows that the minimum size of a small סוכה really is debated: one view accepts "head, most of the body, and table," while רבי demands four by four אמות. So the idea of a dispute over size cannot simply be dismissed.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid; kosher
Four אמות by four אמות: רבי's minimum size

phrases.english: And about a small sukka they do not disagree?
But isn't it taught:
If it holds his head, most of his body, and his table, it is valid.
Rabbi says: Not until it has in it
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: four cubits by four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 11's suggestion that there is no dispute about the size of a small סוכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the argument is about a large סוכה, not about the size of a small one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly records a dispute about a small סוכה's minimum size (head, most of the body, and table versus four by four אמות), so such a dispute clearly exists.

steps.title: A second ברייתא leaves out the table, so the two ברייתות must follow different opinions
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא has the חכמים say that a סוכה holding only head and most of the body is valid, with no mention of the table. This contradicts the first ברייתא, so one must follow בית שמאי and the other בית הלל. That shows there is a dispute about a small סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: רבי says any סוכה that is not four אמות by four אמות is invalid. The חכמים say that even if it holds only his head and most of his body, it is valid. Here 'his table' is not mentioned. The two ברייתות contradict each other. So we must conclude that one follows בית שמאי and the other follows בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to finish its challenge against רב נחמן בר יצחק. It shows that there really is a dispute about how small a סוכה may be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, the חכמים require room for head, most of the body, and the table. In this one, the חכמים require only head and most of the body. The best way to explain the clash is that the first follows בית שמאי (table needed) and the second follows בית הלל (no table needed), so they do argue about a small סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits by four cubits, רבי's minimum size for a סוכה
His head and most of his body
They contradict each other
Learn from it, a way of drawing a conclusion

steps.whyThisMatters: This knocks down רב נחמן בר יצחק's suggestion that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about a big סוכה.

phrases.english: And another ברייתא teaches:
phrases.notes: This is a second ברייתא, different from the one in the last step that mentioned 'his table'.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
Any סוכה that does not have
four cubits by four cubits
is invalid.
And the Sages say:
Even if it holds
only his head and most of his body
it is valid.
But 'his table' is not taught here.
They contradict each other.
Rather, must we not learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: הָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, הָא בֵּית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: this one follows בית שמאי, and that one follows בית הלל.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that requires room for the table follows בית שמאי. The one without the table follows בית הלל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 13 by bringing the contradicting ברייתא and resolving it.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי and בית הלל do argue about the minimum size of a small סוכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות that give the חכמים different minimum sizes, with and without the table.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה also shows the dispute is about the סוכה's size
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא points out that the משנה says בית שמאי 'invalidate' and בית הלל 'validate'. Those words describe the סוכה itself. If the dispute were about how a person sits, the משנה would have said 'he did not fulfill' and 'he fulfilled'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Our משנה is also precise. It says 'בית שמאי invalidate and בית הלל validate.' If the dispute were as רב נחמן בר יצחק said, it should have said 'בית שמאי say he did not fulfill his obligation, and בית הלל say he fulfilled it.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא adds a second proof, this time from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Valid' and 'invalid' describe the סוכה. 'Fulfilled' and 'did not fulfill' describe the person. Since the משנה uses words about the סוכה, the argument must be about the סוכה's size, not about where the person sat.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise, meaning the exact wording supports this reading
Declare invalid / declare valid, words about the object itself
He fulfilled / did not fulfill his obligation, words about the person
It should have said

phrases.english: מר זוטרא said:
Our משנה is also precise,
since it teaches:
'בית שמאי declare it invalid,
and בית הלל declare it valid.'
And if it were so,
phrases.notes: If the argument were about a big סוכה, as רב נחמן בר יצחק suggested.

phrases.english: 'בית שמאי say he did not fulfill his obligation,
and בית הלל say he fulfilled it'
is what it should have said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from the משנה itself to the conclusion of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute in the משנה concerns the validity of a small סוכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words פוסלין and מכשירין, which describe the סוכה rather than the person.

steps.title: But the משנה also says 'one who was'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the dispute is about size, why does the משנה describe a person, 'one who was' with his head and most of his body in the סוכה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the words 'one who was' are difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the new conclusion. Another phrase in the משנה seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One who was' describes where a person is sitting, which fits a big סוכה. This is the point from step 12: a dispute about size would have said 'a סוכה that holds.' So the משנה has wording that supports both readings.

keyTerms.meaning: But then it is difficult
One who was, the משנה's wording describing a person's position

phrases.english: But then it is difficult:
'one who was'!
phrases.notes: These words in the משנה describe where a person is sitting, which sounds like the big-סוכה case from step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 14 and 15 using the wording point from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's dispute is about the size of a small סוכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'one who was' describes a person's position in the סוכה, which fits a big-סוכה case and not a size dispute.

steps.title: They argue about two cases, and the משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about both a small סוכה and a big one. The משנה is missing words and really teaches two separate cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, they argue about two things: a small סוכה and a big סוכה. The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: if someone had his head and most of his body in the סוכה and his table in the house, בית שמאי say he did not fulfill his obligation and בית הלל say he did. And about a סוכה that holds only his head and most of his body, בית שמאי say it is invalid and בית הלל say it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the problem by saying both readings are right. The משנה holds two arguments, and we fill in the missing words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One who was … he did not fulfill / he fulfilled' fits the big-סוכה case, which is about the person. 'Invalid / valid' fits the small-סוכה case, which is about the סוכה itself. Splitting the משנה into two cases explains both sets of wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, used to keep the original position while adjusting it
They argue about two things
The text is missing words
And this is what it teaches
A small סוכה / a big סוכה

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue in two cases. In a big סוכה, if someone sits at the entrance with his table in the house, בית שמאי say he did not fulfill his obligation and בית הלל say he did. In a small סוכה that holds only head and most of the body, בית שמאי say it is invalid and בית הלל say it is valid.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. The 'table in the house' case is a big סוכה and is about the person. The 'holds only head and most of body' case is a small סוכה and is about the סוכה itself.

phrases.english: Actually, they argue about two things:
they argue about a small סוכה,
and they argue about a big סוכה.
And the משנה is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
One whose head and most of his body were in the סוכה
and his table was inside the house,
בית שמאי say: he did not fulfill his obligation,
and בית הלל say: he fulfilled it.
And a סוכה that holds
phrases.notes: Here begins the second case, the small סוכה. These are the words the משנה left out.

phrases.english: only enough for his head and most of his body,
בית שמאי declare it invalid,
and בית הלל declare it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by reading the משנה as two separate disputes.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה (חסורי מיחסרא) so it covers two separate cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes one dispute, either about size or about where a person sits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה contains two disputes: about a person sitting in a big סוכה with his table in the house (יצא / לא יצא), and about a small סוכה's minimum size (פוסלין / מכשירין).

steps.title: Who taught that a house under four by four אמות is not a real house?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind a ברייתא that says a house smaller than four by four אמות is exempt from מזוזה and מעקה, cannot get נגעים, and is not sold for good like houses in walled cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא behind what the רבנן taught: A house that is not four אמות by four אמות is exempt from מזוזה and from a guardrail. It does not become טמא with נגעים. It is not sold permanently the way houses in walled cities are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: which תנא holds that a house smaller than four by four אמות does not count as a house? It quotes a ברייתא to set up the discussion, and the answer will come later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats four by four אמות as the smallest size of a real house. A house smaller than that does not count as a house, so the laws about a 'house' do not apply to it. The גמרא wants to know whose opinion this is, which connects to the four by four אמות measure רבי used for a סוכה in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Four אמות by four אמות, the smallest area of a real house according to this ברייתא
The scroll placed on the doorpost of a house
A guardrail the Torah requires around a flat roof
צרעת-type marks that can make a house טמא
Sold for good, with no going back to the first owner
Houses in walled cities, which have a special sale rule

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'מאן תנא' does not attack anything. The גמרא simply wants to know whose opinion this ברייתא follows.

phrases.english: Who is the תנא who taught this
that the Rabbis taught:
A house that does not have in it
four אמות by four אמות
is exempt from the מזוזה,
and from the guardrail,
and it does not become טמא with נגעים,
and it is not sold for good
like houses in walled cities,
phrases.notes: A house in a walled city can be bought back within a year. After that it stays with the buyer forever (ויקרא 25:29–30).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of a small סוכה, the גמרא moves to a related ברייתא about a house under four by four אמות and asks whose opinion it is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a house smaller than four by four אמות is not legally a house?

steps.title: More laws that do not apply to a tiny house: war and עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues its list. A soldier does not go home from war for such a house. It is not included in עירוב חצרות or שיתוף מבואות, and the עירוב food is not placed in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A soldier does not go back from the battle lines because of such a house. The house is not part of an עירוב, it is not part of a שיתוף, and the עירוב is not placed inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps listing laws that do not apply to a house under four by four אמות. Now it adds the law of going home from war and the laws of עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases follow the same idea as before: a tiny house does not count as a dwelling. So building one does not let a soldier leave the army, and it plays no role in joining courtyards or alleyways for carrying on שבת. Some of these laws are from the Torah and some are rabbinic, yet the same four by four אמות size applies to all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: The battle lines; a man who built a new house may go home from them
Making an עירוב חצרות, joining the houses of a courtyard so people may carry there on שבת
Making a שיתוף מבואות, joining courtyards that open onto an alleyway
The shared food that makes the joining work

phrases.english: and one does not go back because of it
phrases.notes: See דברים 20:5: a man who built a new house goes home from the army. A house this small doesn't count.

phrases.english: from those lined up for war,
and one does not include it in an עירוב,
and one does not include it in a שיתוף,
and one does not place the עירוב in it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא from step 18. It adds more laws that a tiny house is excluded from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house under four by four אמות does not free a soldier from war, and it plays no role in עירוב חצרות or שיתוף מבואות.
